what_was_done: vsdd checkpoint takes an optional --subject that must equal the run record's subject (plan survey.md D1); a mismatch is exit 2 with nothing written, so a strict parser can never strand the lock.
Same fix as P3COV-10: the checkpoint's optional --subject must equal the run record's, exit 2 otherwise, nothing written; W2 still settles what the story script sends (PL3-22).

The survey records every story unit it returns in the run record's stories (admission.admit calls runs.run_admit after the worktree exists), and 'a live run' is one whose run record exists with ended empty, which runs.run_require already refuses on (run_ended).

On the story path: admit called again for a story whose closure carries admitted_by creates nothing new, records the story in the calling run and returns the same unit, so a re-survey in a new run satisfies the gates. The other surveys' re-admission of whole wave maps waits for S3 when widened.

Same admission path as P3REQ-07: the membership check (runs.run_require with story=) is satisfied for a new run because admit re-records the story in the new run; the run live check is the ended field.

Resolved for stories: position() and the evidence lookup read the evidence records of any run — they are written per subject and gate, with no run binding — so a story's position survives the death of its run and a takeover continues from disk. Non-story stages wait for S3 when widened.

No cycle base: admission reads the target branch's head at the moment of creation (target_head) and records it as delivery.base; a later story is cut from the head as it then stands. Readiness ordering (harness chores in wave 1) stays with G5 and the W-feature.

On the story path: the survey's spec_approved precondition shows records' stale detail ('stale') after a hand edit, so the clerk's answer names it. The new route row and the new spec decision the survey opens are not at slice depth; S3 opens them when widened.
where: next/plugins/vsdd-factory/py/vsdd/state/preconditions.py, decisions.py (spec_approved, as built by records); test next/tests/unit/test_preconditions.py::test_spec_stale_after_edit

what_was_done: target_head in pr mode takes the remote from the target branch's upstream (git for-each-ref --format='%(upstream:remotename) %(upstream:remoteref)'), fetches refs/heads/<branch> under the branch's own name and reads the remote-tracking head; an upstream whose ref is not refs/heads/<branch>, and a missing upstream with zero or several remotes, raise WorktreeError('git') naming the branch and the correcting command. No remote name is in code; the test's remote is 'gitea'. Local mode is untouched.

This unit's part: the tracked records this unit writes (closure delivery.branch/base, delivery.run, admitted_by, stage entries) carry no machine-local path — branch names, commit ids and run ids only; the story unit's paths (worktree, story_path, review_rules, test_output) go into the survey's own command output, which may stay absolute. Delivery's closure detail texts are step 4's part.

The assertion the entry reserves for the survey unit: create_story cuts the branch with git branch <name> <commit> (never from a remote-tracking name, never --track) and the test asserts git for-each-ref --format='%(upstream)' prints nothing for the new branch. No push is built; the slice changes nothing on a team.
